output.summary: The district hires Rook Electric, the lowest responsive and responsible bidder, to install 22 new cameras and program 20 existing cameras into the Milestone software at Madison Park Academy. The $75,800 price includes a $10,000 contingency. Work runs 60 days, June 25 through August 14, 2020.

output.headline: Adds $75,970 for summer career-program intern stipends through Oakland Public Education Fund
output.summary: This amendment adds $75,970 to the contract with Oakland Public Education Fund, raising the limit from $200,000 to $275,970. The added money pays more stipends to district student interns in the ECCCO (Exploring College, Career, and Community Options) summer career preparation program. It also extends the contract end date from June 30, 2020 to August 7, 2020.

output.headline: Pays Raskob Day School up to $50,000 for special education services in 2020-21
output.summary: The district signs a master contract with Raskob Day School, a nonpublic, nonsectarian (not religious) school, to provide services to students as set out in the contract. The limit is $50,000 for July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021. The item is part of the Special Education program.

output.headline: Adds $150,000 for Lozano Smith legal services, raising the 2019-20 limit to $450,000
output.summary: This amendment adds $150,000 to the district's agreement with the law firm Lozano Smith for legal help on an as-needed basis. The total for the 2019-20 fiscal year may not exceed $450,000. All other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Adopts the Board of Education's 2020-2021 Governance Handbook
output.summary: The Board adopts its governance handbook for the 2020-2021 year. The text gives no further detail on what the handbook contains.

output.headline: Applies for $318,420 state Workability 1 grant to build work skills for special education students
output.summary: The Board approves the district's Special Education Local Plan Area (SELPA) application to the California Department of Education for $318,420 in Workability 1 funding for 2020-21. The money would support work-readiness skills in the curriculum, career assessments, pre-vocational workshops and job opportunities for students in Programs for Exceptional Children. If the grant is awarded, in whole or in part, the item also authorizes accepting it.

output.headline: Ratifies reappointment of five members to the school facilities bond oversight committee through June 2022
output.summary: The Board ratifies the Board President's reappointment of five eligible members to the Measures A, B, and J Independent Citizens' School Facilities Bond Oversight Committee. Each term ends June 10, 2022.

output.headline: Adopts Measure G1 spending plans and awards totaling $3,916,012 for district and charter middle schools
output.summary: The Board adopts a resolution approving the Measure G1 oversight commission's recommendations for 2020-2021 grant applications and education spending plans at district middle schools and charter middle schools. The awards total $3,916,012.00.

output.headline: Creates or revises job descriptions for 25 district positions
output.summary: The Board adopts Resolution 1920-2037, which creates or revises job descriptions across Nutrition Services, Buildings and Grounds, Linked Learning, Technology Services, Early Childhood Education, Police Services and other departments. The 25 positions include Plumbers Helper, Production Cook, four levels of Student Information Systems Specialist and Early Literacy Reading Tutor. The text lists no dollar amount.

output.headline: Amends the 2020-21 layoffs and additions of classified (non-teaching) positions
output.summary: The Board adopts Resolution 1920-2026B, which amends the 2020-21 plan for layoffs and additions of classified (non-teaching) positions. It provides for reducing or laying off positions, and for reinstating, increasing or creating positions, based on lack of funds or program need in the 2020-21 budget process. The text lists no dollar amount.

output.headline: Hires Waste Management for trash, recycling and compost service, up to $3.25M a year
output.summary: The district signs a general services agreement with Waste Management of Alameda County, Inc. for solid waste, recycling and composting collection and related services at set rates. Spending is capped at $3,250,000 per year. The agreement has two one-year options to extend, and the text does not state a start or end date.

vendor.name: Waste Management of Alameda County, Inc.

output.headline: Revises the 2020-21 school calendar to add an Oakland Educator Wellness Day on May 10, 2021
output.summary: The Board approves a revised 2020-21 school calendar. The revision adds an Oakland Educator Wellness Day on May 10, 2021, a non-duty day for employees at 10-month school sites, and includes marking period dates.

output.headline: Pays SchoolMint up to $198,500 for school-choice application and registration software in 2020-21
output.summary: The district signs a software-as-a-service agreement with SchoolMint for hosting, maintenance, upgrades and support of its School Finder products, including the district choice application and lottery and registration, plus a data link with the Aeries student system. The period is July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021. The amount is capped at $198,500.

output.headline: Directs the Board secretary to cast the district's ballot in a 2020 school boards association runoff election
output.summary: This resolution instructs the Board's secretary to cast a ballot for one candidate in the California School Boards Association 2020 Delegate Assembly runoff for Sub-Region 7-B (Alameda County). The ballot must be returned by August 11, 2020.
